note: Hand-written metadata (URLs, licences, platform notes). Hashes, counts and length statistics are NOT here: build_manifest.py recomputes them from the data directory. Checked 2026-10-05 against the Zenodo, ENA and GitHub APIs.

cnr.name: Clustered Nanopore Reads (CNR)
cnr.publication: Srinivasavaradhan, Gopi, Pfister, Yekhanin. Trellis BMA: coded trace reconstruction on IDS channels for DNA storage. ISIT 2021, arXiv:2107.06440
cnr.licence: MIT (GitHub API and LICENSE file); keep copyright and licence notice when reusing
cnr.usage_constraints: Dataset README note of 2024-08-12: the 10,000 centres are not uniformly random (long-range dependencies from a generation error), so clustering may have produced malformed clusters. Empty clusters mean dropout or clustering failure (not distinguishable).
cnr.platform: Twist Bioscience synthesis, PCR, Oxford Nanopore MinION (LQK-LSK109 ligation kit); basecaller not stated
cnr.library_prep: Amplified products ligated to ONT adapters; reads clustered with the algorithm of Rashtchian et al. (NIPS 2017)
cnr.data_state: processed: basecalled reads, already clustered by reference (reference = cluster centre); original FASTQ not published
cnr.coverage_note: Per-cluster read counts are in the manifest (cluster_size); reads are pre-clustered so coverage per reference is observed directly, but clustering drops outlier reads

dt4dds-twist.name: DT4DDS Twist_GCfix Aging_0a / 0b replicates, plus PhiX spike-in run (R1 only)
dt4dds-twist.source: ENA project PRJEB65931 (INSDC); design FASTA from GitHub fml-ethz/dt4dds_notebooks
dt4dds-twist.publication: Gimpel et al. Characterizing and mitigating errors and biases in DNA data storage (DT4DDS). Nat Commun 14:6026 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41467-023-41729-1
dt4dds-twist.licence: Reads: INSDC, no explicit licence (INSDC places no restriction on use). Design FASTA: dt4dds_notebooks repository has no licence, so it must not be committed or redistributed; only its SHA-256 and counts are recorded. dt4dds code is GPL-3.0: external tool only, never copied into this MIT tree
dt4dds-twist.usage_constraints: Only R1 of each paired run is downloaded (R2 not used in this step). Design FASTA of Aging_0a is used for both 0a and 0b (same Twist_GCfix pool design per the registry; not verified for 0b separately). PhiX run has no designed strands: reference is the PhiX174 genome (NC_001422.1, 5,386 bp, not downloaded here)
dt4dds-twist.platform: Twist Bioscience synthesis (GC-constrained pool, 12,000 designs x 108 nt data region), KAPA PCR, Illumina iSeq 100 2x150 (reads also contain priming regions)
dt4dds-twist.library_prep: Aging_0a/0b are the unaged baselines (replicates); PhiX run is the matching sequencing-only control
dt4dds-twist.data_state: raw: demultiplexed FASTQ from ENA, unmapped, untrimmed
dt4dds-twist.coverage_note: Raw reads are not assigned to references in this step; nominal_reads_per_design = reads / designs is a depth proxy only

d03-nanopore.name: Nanopore end-to-end coding scheme experimental data (clustered read segments, passQ-true groups)
d03-nanopore.publication: Welter, Sokolovskii, Heinis, Wachter-Zeh, Rosnes, Graell i Amat. An End-to-End Coding Scheme for DNA-Based Data Storage With Nanopore-Sequenced Reads. IEEE J. Sel. Areas Inf. Theory 7:17-32 (2026), doi:10.1109/JSAIT.2026.3655592; arXiv:2406.12955
d03-nanopore.usage_constraints: Segments with |drift| > 15 nt or missing primers were excluded by the authors, so the edit-distance tail and truncation are under-observed. Groups are disjoint read sets of the same oligo pool: references repeat across files and groups, so a reference-disjoint split must be made on reference sequence, not on file. Whole archive is 138 MB (below the 2 GB limit), so it was downloaded.
d03-nanopore.platform: GenScript synthesis, PCR, Oxford Nanopore MinION; guppy basecalling, accurate (acc=true) vs fast (acc=false); passQ-true = reads passing the Q>=8 filter
d03-nanopore.library_prep: Strand = 20-nt primer + 110-nt payload + 20-nt primer = 150 nt; forward and backward (reverse-complemented orientation) segments are separate files
d03-nanopore.data_state: processed: basecalled reads, primer-located and segmented, clustered by nearest reference (Levenshtein); FASTQ not included
d03-nanopore.coverage_note: Per-cluster read counts are in the manifest; empty clusters are listed per file

d13-lopez-nanopore.name: Lopez et al. 2019 nanopore readout of assembled DNA-storage oligos (registry D13)
metadata_urls: https://api.github.com/repos/uwmisl/data-ncomms19-nanopore/contents/<run file> (Git LFS pointer: sha256 oid and size)
d13-lopez-nanopore.publication: Lopez R, Chen YJ, Dumas Ang S, Yekhanin S, Makarychev K, Racz MZ, Seelig G, Strauss K, Ceze L. DNA assembly for nanopore data storage readout. Nat Commun 10:2933 (2019), doi:10.1038/s41467-019-10978-4 (PMC6610119)
d13-lopez-nanopore.licence: NONE STATED: the GitHub repository has no licence file (GitHub API: license null; /license 404, checked 2026-10-05). The article is open access, but that licence covers the article, not this repository. Treated as all rights reserved: internal use only
d13-lopez-nanopore.usage_constraints: Founder approval 2026-10-05 for internal use. Never commit or redistribute reads, reference sequences or per-read derived data (read segments, alignments, per-reference coverage); only aggregate statistics (rates, histograms, counts) may be published, with attribution to the article. Run 13 (space_shuttle) is the held-out file under docs/V7_PROTOCOL_AMENDMENT_D3.md (PR-3.1); before a PREREG commit it is opened only by this manifest script, for its hash and a gzip integrity check
d13-lopez-nanopore.platform: Twist Bioscience synthesis; PCR random access with overhang primers, then Gibson assembly (apollo: 24 fragments, ~4.6 kb) or overlap-extension PCR (365-dishes: 10 groups); ONT MinION, R9.4 flow cells, 1D^2 ligation kit LSK-308, one flow cell per file (apollo: two, runs 15 and 18), 48 h; only 1D^2 reads are in the files (read IDs are two concatenated UUIDs). Basecaller and version are not stated in the article or in the FASTQ headers
d13-lopez-nanopore.library_prep: Each reference is a 150-nt oligo: 20-nt file primer + 110-nt payload with address + 20-nt file primer (verified in the reference files: one primer pair per file, ten for 365-dishes). Reads are of assembled concatemers: several oligos of one file per read, joined by the assembly overhangs, in either orientation
d13-lopez-nanopore.data_state: basecalled 1D^2 reads (FASTQ, gzip), not demultiplexed into oligos; reference oligo lists per file (text, 5'-SEQ-3' per line); mapping file -> run in read_me_data-ncomms19-nanopore.txt
d13-lopez-nanopore.coverage_note: Article: apollo 267,152 1D^2 reads, on average 17.99 payload alignments per read, 43x mean coverage over 102,084 payloads; reported error rate 6.87 % from alignment (THEORETICAL here: published numbers, not reproduced by this manifest)

cas9-random-access.name: Imburgia et al. 2025 Cas9 random access, nanopore reads of rolling-circle concatemers (registry CAS9)
cas9-random-access.source_commit: 03f029cac35896d6abf0ab339ec89b031830b72c (main, 2022-07-04; the head at download; reads fetched at this commit by fetch_d3.py)
download_urls: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/uwmisl/cas9-random-access/main/20200715_basecalled_reads/<288 files listed by the GitHub contents API>
cas9-random-access.publication: Imburgia C, Organick L, Zhang K, Cardozo N, McBride J, Bee C, Wilde D, Roote G, Jorgensen S, Ward D, Anderson C, Strauss K, Ceze L, Nivala J. Random access and semantic search in DNA data storage enabled by Cas9 and machine-guided design. Nat Commun 16:6388 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61264-5 (PMC12246221); Author Correction Nat Commun 17:1455 (2026)
cas9-random-access.accession: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15499096 (code snapshot v0.0, 3.3 GB zip; not downloaded)
cas9-random-access.licence: NONE in the GitHub repository (no licence file; GitHub API license null, checked 2026-10-05). The Zenodo snapshot record declares cc-by-4.0 in its metadata; the article is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The bundled C3POa (software/, GPL-2.0) and BLAT are third-party code: not downloaded, never copied. Treated as all rights reserved for the GitHub copy: internal use only
cas9-random-access.usage_constraints: Founder approval 2026-10-05 for internal use. Only 20200715_basecalled_reads (288 FASTQ, stored gzip-compressed) and three small files are downloaded; the 4 GB 20200715_results directory is not. Never commit reads or per-read derived data; aggregate statistics only. The designed strands (25 files, ~1.6 M strands) are NOT published in the repository, so there is no ground-truth reference: error statistics are against a leave-one-out consensus of each read's own repeat units (docs/V7_PROTOCOL_AMENDMENT_D3.md), basis 'inferred'. File 13 (address g13) is held out (PR-3.2): its reads are classified by address, counted and not otherwise used
cas9-random-access.platform: Twist Bioscience synthesis (25 files, ~1.6 M strands, 165 nt: 20-nt Cas9 address overlapping the universal forward primer + 125-nt payload + 20-nt universal reverse primer); Gibson assembly into a circle, rolling-circle amplification (R2C2 design), Cas9 cleavage of files 2, 13, 24, adapter ligation; ONT R9.4.1 flow cells; Guppy v3.2.2 with a quality-score cutoff of 9 (article Methods)
cas9-random-access.library_prep: Reads are concatemers of repeat units of one circularised molecule; the article's pipeline (C3POa) demultiplexes by file address and calls a per-read consensus. Address sequences per file: splint_all.fasta (24 nt; common 14-nt prefix)
cas9-random-access.data_state: basecalled reads that passed the Q9 filter (FASTQ split in 288 chunks of one run), not demultiplexed
cas9-random-access.coverage_note: No designed-strand list: coverage per strand cannot be computed. Reads per file address can (characterisation)
